title: Gut and Sleep Diary
description: A one-week diary for hours of sleep, stress, and gut symptoms. It opens with a clearly labeled, made-up sample week for Sam (a fictional student with IBS), plots the data over time and as a scatter plot, reports the correlation between sleep and gut symptoms, and warns about small samples and stress as a confounder. All data stays in the page's memory only; nothing is stored or sent.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: neuroscience (gut-brain axis)
publisher: Gut Check: The Neuroscience of How Your Gut and Brain Talk
learningObjectives: Record or explore a one-week diary of sleep, stress, and gut symptoms and describe the pattern between sleep and symptoms using the correlation coefficient r.
Judge the limits of personal diary data, including small sample size, confounders such as stress, and the possibility of reverse causation.
prerequisites: Reading a bar chart and a scatter plot
The idea that correlation does not prove cause (Chapter 1, the six questions)
keyQuestions: Do Sam's gut symptoms rise on days after less sleep?
Could stress explain both poor sleep and worse gut symptoms?
How much can one unusual day change the correlation in a one-week diary?
What would a fairer test of sleep and gut symptoms look like?
misconceptions: If a symptom diary shows a pattern, you have found the cause.
A strong correlation in one week of data is reliable.
Correlation always runs in the direction you expect (sleep affects gut, never gut affects sleep).
One factor at a time is all that changes from day to day.
privacy: Data is kept in memory only. No localStorage, cookies, or network requests; reloading the page erases all entries.
